The last alternative considered was to set either a higher or a lower standard. A higher standard could result in more savings in petroleum for those vehicles of no more than 6,000 pounds GVWR. However, all of the market shift concerns expressed for the third alternative apply and if either vehicles or consumer purchases are shifted to the over 6,000 pounds GVWR class, a reduction in fleet fuel economy could result, since those vehicles over 6,000 pounds GVWR will in general have lower fuel economy. The agency did not have an objective means of assessing the probability of these market shifts but their consideration led to the AFES. It is the agency's position that this reflects the "maximum feasible average fuel economy" for nonpassenger automobiles of no more than 6,000 pounds GVWR for model year 1979.
A lower standard was rejected because it would result in lower fuel economy for those NPA's of no more than 6,000 pounds GVWR. Since the Act requires "maximum feasible average fuel economy" a lower standard would not be consonant with the requirement of the Act.
